candidates.attacker_control: The boundary token is taken verbatim from the attacker-supplied `Content-Type` header (`FileUploadBase.getBoundary`, lines 419-436, via ParameterParser) and passed to `new MultipartStream(input, boundary, notifier)` (FileUploadBase.java:988-994). The request body bytes, connection lifetime and body length are also attacker-controlled. No application-specific value is needed: any endpoint that routes multipart requests through FileUploadBase.parseRequest/getItemIterator/ServletFileUpload exposes this path before any file content is validated.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Searched all uses of `boundaryLength` in the tree: it is only mutated by setBoundary (which merely requires equal length for nested boundaries, MultipartStream.java:497-505) and temporarily by skipPreamble (625-643, keepRegion is not reduced there); there is no length cap. getBoundary and ParameterParser perform no length validation. The constructor contains neither the upstream null check nor the bufSize-vs-boundaryLength guard, confirming the vulnerable revision (the 1.3-era CVE-2013-0248 repository validation in DiskFileItem.readObject is present, placing the snapshot before the 1.3.1 parser fix). Verified by invariant analysis that with keepRegion < bufSize (short boundaries) a full buffer yields pad = keepRegion < bufSize so available() > 0 and makeAvailable returns, i.e. the hang specifically requires the missing guard and an oversized boundary, not ordinary uploads. Checked that no test/configuration in the snapshot constrains boundary length or the buffer size (no test references the constructor's buffer argument with an oversized boundary).
candidates.impact: Unauthenticated remote denial of service. A single crafted multipart request pins a request-processing thread in an unbounded CPU-consuming loop that never returns and never throws; repeating or parallelizing requests starves the container thread pool / exhausts CPU. The thread cannot be recovered by request timeouts or by socket-level interruption because the loop performs no I/O and no further reads after the buffer is full; the affected worker must be killed (e.g. container restart). Default FileUpload configuration has no request size limit (sizeMax = -1), so no application-side limit blocks this path in the common case.
candidates.prerequisites: 1) Application uses this revision to parse multipart requests (ServletFileUpload/FileUploadBase with DiskFileUpload or the streaming API). 2) Parser uses the default 4096-byte buffer, or a custom bufSize <= boundaryLength (same defect class whenever the missing guard is absent). 3) The boundary parameter is at least bufSize - 4 bytes (>= 4092 for the default buffer); the servlet container must accept a ~4 KB Content-Type header (typical default limits, e.g. 8 KB, allow this). 4) The attacker supplies at least bufSize bytes of body that do not contain a complete delimiter match at the front; because findSeparator's search window is clamped to `maxpos = tail - boundaryLength` (<= 2 positions for such a boundary), an exact match is effectively impossible to hit, and keeping the connection open guarantees the buffer fill. 5) sizeMax is -1 (the default, FileUploadBase.java:161) or >= the bytes needed to fill the buffer; a small sizeMax instead raises SizeLimitExceededException during the fill, before the loop. Once the buffer is full, the loop performs no further reads, so sizeMax/fileSizeMax can no longer interrupt it.
candidates.root_cause: MultipartStream's constructor (src/main/java/org/apache/commons/fileupload/MultipartStream.java:323-344) sizes internal state directly from the caller-supplied boundary with no length guard: `boundaryLength = boundary.length + 4` (line 335) and `keepRegion = this.boundary.length` (line 336, i.e. keepRegion == boundaryLength), while the buffer is only `bufSize` bytes (default DEFAULT_BUFSIZE = 4096, line 184/358-362). Nothing enforces `bufSize >= boundaryLength + 1`. When boundaryLength >= bufSize, ItemInputStream.findSeparator() (lines 817-826) can only ever set `pad = min(keepRegion, tail-head)`, so `available()` (lines 846-851) is 0 whenever the buffer is full; MultipartStream.findSeparator() (lines 697-718) computes `maxpos = tail - boundaryLength <= 0`, so a complete delimiter cannot be matched once tail reaches bufSize. makeAvailable() (lines 983-1017) then executes `input.read(buffer, tail, bufSize - tail)` with `bufSize - tail == 0`; InputStream.read(byte[],int,int) returns 0 for len 0, so `tail` never advances, `available()` stays 0 and `pos` stays -1, and the `for(;;)` loop at lines 996-1016 never exits. The parser neither throws nor blocks; it burns CPU indefinitely.
candidates.title: MultipartStream accepts oversized boundary and spins forever in ItemInputStream.makeAvailable (zero-length read loop) — remote DoS
candidates.trace: FileItemIteratorImpl constructor: `contentType = ctx.getContentType()` (FileUploadBase.java:944) -> `boundary = getBoundary(contentType)` with no length limit (988, 419-436) -> `multi = new MultipartStream(input, boundary, notifier)` with DEFAULT_BUFSIZE=4096 (994; MultipartStream.java:358-362, 184). Constructor stores keepRegion = boundaryLength = boundary.length + 4 with no bufSize check (MultipartStream.java:334-336). First `findNextItem()` (FileUploadBase.java:1007-1021) calls `multi.skipPreamble()` (MultipartStream.java:624-644) -> `discardBodyData()` (610-613) -> `readBodyData(null)` (586-590) -> `newInputStream()` -> `ItemInputStream`; `Streams.copy`/`read()` drive `available()`/`makeAvailable()` (MultipartStream.java:865-911, 983-1017). When tail reaches bufSize without a match, `pad = tail - head = bufSize` (817-826), `available() == 0` (846-851), and `input.read(buffer, bufSize, 0)` returns 0 forever (997), so the loop at 996-1016 never terminates; the same state is reachable via `multi.discardBodyData()` for later parts (FileUploadBase.java:1071), via item content reads (`Streams.copy(item.openStream(), ...)`, FileUploadBase.java:347), and via ItemInputStream.close()/skip() (MultipartStream.java:930-975).
candidates.unverified: No code was executed and no runtime confirmation was possible. The concrete container header-size ceiling for the Content-Type value (needs ~4 KB) and whether a particular embedding application sets sizeMax below ~4 KB or supplies a custom MultipartStream buffer larger than the boundary are environment-dependent and were not verified. Java InputStream.read(byte[],int,int) length-0 semantics were reasoned from the documented contract, not exercised. The exact upstream fix commit was not consulted (no patches/metadata available in this run); the described defect was derived solely from this source snapshot.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-835: Loop with Unreachable Exit Condition ('Infinite Loop'); CWE-400: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption

coverage_summary: Model-visible scope: 74 files (75 source-root entries; 1 excluded by the sensitive-name/path filter, 0 binaries/symlinks excluded at the 5 MiB limit). The P1 relation index catalogues the same 74 files but is explicitly partial: only 11 Java files parsed, 12 omitted, 639 symbols/1231 edges, with control-flow, data-flow and semantic resolution not implemented and 901 unresolved calls; index entries (including the call edges into ItemInputStream.makeAvailable) were used only for navigation and every claim above was verified against the source text. I read in full or in substantial part the core request-processing classes: MultipartStream (constructor, boundary/body parsing, ItemInputStream), FileUploadBase (getBoundary, getItemIterator, FileItemIteratorImpl, parseRequest, size limits), ParameterParser, DiskFileItem (including write/readObject/writeObject), Streams, LimitedInputStream and both mime decoders; I skimmed ServletFileUpload/ServletRequestContext, the factories and the test classes for boundary/size-related cases. Build metadata (pom.xml, RELEASE-NOTES.txt) was read only for version context.
limitations: No execution, compilation, unit tests, scanning or dynamic analysis was performed; all conclusions are static source reading, and the candidate is a lead, not a confirmed vulnerability.
The P1 index is partial (11/74 files parsed, 12 omitted, no data-flow/control-flow or semantic resolution); unreported areas are not claimed as reviewed.
Portlet package files, the file-item factory classes and parts of util/mime were only skimmed; a deeper issue there cannot be excluded.
Reachability depends on how a consuming application wires FileUpload (buffer size, sizeMax, whether multipart parsing is invoked before authentication); these are outside the snapshot.
Container-level limits (maximum HTTP header size) that gate the oversized Content-Type value were not verifiable from this repository.

rejected_leads.lead: DiskFileItem serialization round-trip (readObject builds an OutputStream and copies dfosFile content, DiskFileItem.java:635-693)
rejected_leads.reason: Attacker control requires the embedding application to deserialize attacker-supplied bytes into a DiskFileItem (Java deserialization precondition), not merely to receive an upload, so it is neither reachable through the multipart parser nor self-contained. The revision already validates the repository path (directory + NUL check, lines 666-679), and any information-disclosure/path effect depends on how the application exposes the deserialized item. Kept as unconfirmed; substantially weaker than the remotely triggered parser loop.

rejected_leads.reason: Produces a NullPointerException and a failed request (500) at most; no memory corruption or resource exhaustion beyond a single rejected request, and the constructor-level finding dominates.

summary: Apache Commons FileUpload snapshot (pom 1.4-SNAPSHOT, release notes for 1.3). The strongest source-evidenced issue is in the multipart parser: `MultipartStream` accepts an arbitrarily long boundary token for its 4096-byte working buffer, and `ItemInputStream.makeAvailable()` then enters a zero-progress busy loop (`input.read(buffer, bufSize, 0)` returns 0 forever while `available()` stays 0), giving a remote denial of service. This is the CVE-2014-0050-class defect (oversized boundary / infinite loop) and the guard that later releases added (`bufSize` vs `boundaryLength`) is absent from the constructor. Other leads (DiskFileItem deserialization write path, null sub-boundary NPE) are much weaker and are listed as rejected. No code was executed; findings are source-level only.
